trust_decision.summary: Whether a backend may trust an identity header (BasicAuth/DigestAuth headerField, ForwardAuth authResponseHeaders) that Traefik manages only in its dash/canonical form; at the pinned commit the auth middlewares delete only the canonical key, so a client-sent underscore variant (X_Auth_User) reaches backends that fold '_' to '-'. The published fix decides this at the entry point, via a new opt-in static option (default keep) that deletes or rejects every underscore header before routing.

landing_point.why: The summary names BasicAuth/DigestAuth/ForwardAuth headerField; this is where headerField is deleted with Header.Del (canonical key only) and re-set. The existing underscore-aware defence for X-Forwarded headers (pkg/middlewares/forwardedheaders/forwarded_header.go:52-65) also points a reader at per-middleware fixes.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/server/server_entrypoint_tcp.go:600-602 (createHTTPServer handler chain, package pkg/server) plus pkg/config/static/entrypoints.go:63-78 — the published fix lives here, not in pkg/middlewares/auth where the report leads

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Underscores are legal header-name characters and Traefik already Del()s the configured header; folding '_' into '-' is the backend's (CGI/WSGI/PHP) quirk, so a solver can argue the auth middlewares are correct and an entry-point-wide filter (or any change to default behaviour) is out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Requests carrying legitimate underscore-named headers must still be forwarded unchanged by default (keep is the default and documented as preserving behaviour), and under delete the legitimate dash-form X-Auth-User must survive while only the underscore variant is dropped; an unconditional strip/reject breaks the keep default and the integration test expecting 409 under keep.

strategy values: unset/empty, keep, delete, reject, invalid value -> startup error (fix.diff:371-380)
